ranking_method.warning: Weighted scores rank information-gathering work. They are not ROI, probability, revenue, or profit forecasts.
ranking_method.tie_break: lower falsification cost, then faster evidence, then stable ID

items.title: Apify pay-per-event official-data Actors
items.mechanism: Users or software agents pay per result or event for normalized public-source data selected from measured Store demand gaps.
items.payer_source_of_value: Customers avoid source integration, normalization, maintenance, metering, and delivery work.
items.capital_requirement: USD 0 for public telemetry/local prototype; account, plan, and publication are later gates.
items.expected_economics: Platform monetization exists, but provider revenue, paid event volume, churn, costs, and contribution margin are unobserved.
items.largest_uncertainty: Whether visible users generate sufficient paid volume for a differentiated, permitted-source wedge.
items.evidence_quality: high for public usage/pricing telemetry; low for revenue and retention
items.falsification_cost_time: USD 0 direct cost; initial snapshot minutes, momentum window seven daily observations.
items.security_operational_risk: medium: source changes, CAPTCHA, quality, privacy, and maintenance; no external execution during research.
items.legal_compliance_friction: medium: source terms, public-record privacy, and false assurance claims require a source gate.
items.competition: medium-high; search is noisy and several niches have established Actors.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: Capture and compare seven daily public Store snapshots, curate exact substitutes, then apply the demand/differentiation/source gate.
items.promotion_gate: At least 20 aggregate 30-day users, one paid relevant Actor with at least 5 users, fewer than five credible substitutes above that level, a defensible output gap, and permitted stable source access.
rejection_criteria: Curated telemetry is flat or declining.
Plausible volume cannot support USD 100 monthly contribution margin.

items.title: SEC filing-diff and event API
items.mechanism: Developers and analysts pay for point-in-time filing changes, extracted events, amendment provenance, and alerts rather than raw EDGAR records.
items.payer_source_of_value: Integration time, correctness, latency, normalized schemas, and maintained provenance.
items.capital_requirement: USD 0 for public SEC ingestion and local fixtures; hosting/billing are later gates.
items.expected_economics: Paid providers exist, but raw SEC access and free listings make an undifferentiated proxy uneconomic; customer count is unobserved.
items.largest_uncertainty: Whether a narrow diff/event output creates value not already supplied by free or mature alternatives.
items.evidence_quality: high for source rules; medium for pricing; low for buyer demand
items.falsification_cost_time: USD 0 and one to three days for a 100-issuer local fixture.
items.security_operational_risk: medium: financial-data correctness, rate control, revision/look-ahead errors, and timeliness.
items.legal_compliance_friction: medium: attribution, redistribution, liability, and source policy.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: Generate point-in-time diffs for 100 issuers from public data; compare output fields, correctness, and latency with alternatives.
rejection_criteria: Output is trivial over raw EDGAR.
reopening_criteria: New buyer evidence identifies an underserved workflow.

items.title: Atlassian Forge/Rovo access-evidence assistant
items.mechanism: Administrators pay per licensed user for access reviews, permission evidence, remediation tracking, and auditor-ready exports.
items.payer_source_of_value: Reduced compliance evidence labor and safer remediation.
items.capital_requirement: Low for research/local prototype; billing, agreement, and security review are later gates.
items.expected_economics: Per-user billing supports recurring revenue, but installs do not reveal paid retention and the category is crowded.
items.largest_uncertainty: Whether a narrow repeated workflow gap exists despite mature incumbents.
items.evidence_quality: high for platform economics; medium for install signals; low for retention
items.falsification_cost_time: USD 0 and two to four days of public listing/review analysis.
items.security_operational_risk: medium-high: OAuth scopes, customer data, evidence correctness, support, and review.
items.legal_compliance_friction: medium: privacy, GDPR, marketplace terms, and audit claims.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: Mine 100 competitors/reviews; proceed only if a repeated complaint is absent from top incumbents and solvable with narrow scopes.
rejection_criteria: Scopes or support/security cost dominate plausible MRR.
reopening_criteria: New Rovo capability or clear narrow-workflow growth.

items.title: Shopify catalog-quality anomaly monitor
items.mechanism: Merchants pay monthly for detection and controlled remediation of catalog-quality anomalies.
items.payer_source_of_value: Reduced manual catalog work and fewer revenue-impacting defects.
items.capital_requirement: USD 0 for research/synthetic fixtures; publication later requires registration and hosting.
items.expected_economics: Subscriptions can recur, but adjacent apps are inexpensive and usage/revenue evidence is sparse.
items.largest_uncertainty: Differentiation and retained merchant willingness to pay.
items.evidence_quality: high for platform economics; medium-low for demand
items.falsification_cost_time: USD 0 and two to three days.
items.security_operational_risk: medium-high: merchant data, write scopes, and erroneous bulk edits.
items.legal_compliance_friction: medium: privacy, marketplace review, support, and terms.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: Map complaints, permissions, pricing, and gaps across 50 listings; build only a read-only checker with synthetic fixtures.
rejection_criteria: Five or more credible adopted apps already solve the wedge without unresolved complaints.
reopening_criteria: New Shopify data surface or strong merchant signal.

items.title: Algora code-bounty worker
items.mechanism: Maintainers pay a fixed bounty for a merged public issue solution.
items.automation_potential: medium; engineering can be assisted, but access/claim/submission cannot be assumed.
items.capital_requirement: USD 0; terms and account/legal actions are binding constraints.
items.expected_economics: Historical awards exist, but sampled current supply is thin and recurring revenue is weak.
items.largest_uncertainty: Sufficient live supply and permission for automated access.
items.evidence_quality: high for sampled awards/published terms; low for platform-wide supply
items.falsification_cost_time: Read-only GitHub research is free; automated Algora discovery is stopped.
items.security_operational_risk: medium-high: untrusted repositories, duplicate work, dependency execution, low hourly value.
items.legal_compliance_friction: high: published terms prohibit robot/spider access; account creation accepts legal terms.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: No automated access. Reassess only with written permission or revised terms; then locally test one manually selected issue without claim/submission.
rejection_criteria: Eligible supply cannot support USD 1,000 monthly at realistic completion rates.
reopening_criteria: Written permission/revised terms plus stronger live supply.

items.title: AI-assisted smart-contract audit pipeline
items.mechanism: Protocols pay accepted rewards for privately disclosed reproducible vulnerabilities.
items.automation_potential: medium; analysis can be automated, expert review/disclosure remain mandatory.
items.expected_economics: Maximum rewards are large but outcomes are skewed; duplicates/invalid reports pay zero.
items.largest_uncertainty: Novel valid finding rate after false-positive and duplicate filtering.
items.evidence_quality: high for program/rule/reward data; absent for this system's hit rate
items.falsification_cost_time: USD 0 and three to seven days for one fixed-budget offline audit.
items.security_operational_risk: very high: sensitive vulnerabilities, unsafe proofs, disclosure timing, harm.
items.legal_compliance_friction: high: program rules, KYC/sanctions, scope, disclosure.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: Run one isolated offline audit, measure analyzer precision/reproduction, retain findings securely, do not submit.
rejection_criteria: Mostly known/false findings after a fixed 40-hour budget.
reopening_criteria: Stronger analyzer, new protocol version, or new scope.

items.title: CoW Protocol solver optimization
items.mechanism: A solver competes to improve batch-auction execution and may receive protocol-aligned rewards.
items.payer_source_of_value: Improved settlement quality and solver competition.
items.capital_requirement: Zero for replay; live operation needs infrastructure, bond, signer, gas/liquidity, and unavailable Governor authority.
items.expected_economics: Reward mechanics exist, but this system has no measured edge and live net economics are unknown.
items.largest_uncertainty: Whether optimization beats incumbents net of gas, latency, reverts, and risk.
items.evidence_quality: high for mechanics; zero for proprietary edge
items.falsification_cost_time: USD 0 direct cost and roughly one week for at least 10,000 public auction replays.
items.security_operational_risk: very high: bond, gas, inventory, settlement, MEV, latency, approvals, signing.
items.legal_compliance_friction: high for eventual financial operation; replay remains permitted.
items.next_falsifiable_experiment: Replay at least 10,000 auctions against a baseline with gas, latency cutoffs, reverts, and rank distributions.
rejection_criteria: No stable score improvement survives execution costs or latency.
reopening_criteria: Reward changes, new liquidity, or new optimization mechanism.
